problems.statement: Presenting hypothesis: zero deviations and Line 3's 118% attainment reflect genuine quality ownership and a best-practice model that can be rolled out.

The supervisor bonus penalty (4% per attributed deviation, up to 40%) created an incentive to suppress NCRs, so zero deviations is a measurement artifact of the reporting incentive, not an absence of defects.
Line 3's output is inflated by undocumented labor borrowed from Lines 1 and 4 (about 5.3 technicians per day); per technician-hour productivity is unchanged, so there is no better method to template.

Line 3 is concealing leaking or mis-bonded units through off-record rework in the back cage, with no NCR or device history record entry. Supported by an anonymous report and indirect signals, but not directly verified.

The real quality state is deteriorating: customer complaints (11 to 31 ppm) and final-inspection rejections (0.8% to 1.3%) are rising, concentrated in luer bond leaks traced to Line 3 lots. This is an unreported patient-safety and regulatory exposure.
A weak speak-up climate and an ineffective escalation channel (fear of retaliation, night-shift moves, ethics case closed on the accused supervisor's denial) means silence is not evidence of health.
The Quality Manager's claim that the new first-pass training program caused the drop in deviations.

The root luer bond cure-time variability identified in 2025 was never fixed (CAPA-2025-117 open, no bonding-station change), so the underlying defect persists and Line 3 remains the leading source of leaks.
The lower-cost tubing supplier introduced in April 2026 explains the quality decline or the extra purchasing.
Line 3's 'tight' practices (5S, huddles) explain its superior performance.
Leadership (Plant Manager and HR) designed the incentive and closed the ethics case internally, so they are conflicted, and the Plant Manager's account is not independent.

causalClaims.from: Supervisor bonus deduction per attributed deviation (effective Feb 2026)
causalClaims.to: Collapse of deviation reports to zero
Off-record rework and hidden defects on Line 3
Declines in Line 1 and Line 4 plan attainment

causalClaims.from: Unaddressed luer bond cure-time variability (open CAPA)
causalClaims.to: Luer bond leaks and customer complaints

causalClaims.from: Fear of retaliation and closed ethics case
causalClaims.to: Absence of quality reports and silence of staff

actions.action: Decline to adopt Line 3 as the plant template and do not roll out its practices to Lines 1, 2, 4 and 5.
actions.rationale: Its apparent advantage is explained by borrowed labor, unchanged productivity per technician-hour, and likely hidden defects, so replication would spread the artifact.

actions.action: Suspend the per-deviation supervisor bonus deduction and replace it with metrics that do not punish reporting, such as including independent QC and complaint outcomes.
actions.rationale: It is the established mechanism suppressing reporting; removing it is reversible and addresses the cause.

actions.action: Have Regulatory Affairs or an independent party reopen ethics case 2026-031 and audit Line 3: back-cage walk-through, device history records against component consumption, and review of units built since June.
actions.rationale: It cheaply resolves the key uncertainty (off-record rework) and the case was closed without any records review.

actions.action: Escalate the complaint and rejection trend through the quality system: assess Line 3 lots shipped since February, consider containment, and evaluate customer notification and regulatory reporting obligations.
actions.rationale: Leak complaints trace to Line 3 lots and may carry patient-safety and regulatory consequences, so delay is risky.

actions.action: Close CAPA-2025-117 on luer bonding cure-time variability with a real process fix and change control.
actions.rationale: It is the unaddressed technical root cause of leaks and has been open for a year.

actions.action: Document and formalize or stop the informal technician lending, and correct line-level attainment and cost attribution.
actions.rationale: Hidden labor transfers distort line performance data and unfairly penalize Lines 1 and 4.

actions.action: Discipline or identify the Line 4 supervisor's source, the hotline reporter, or Line 3 staff before facts are established; punish supervisors based on the allegation alone.
actions.rationale: Punishing messengers or acting on an unverified allegation chills reporting further and may hit the wrong party.

actions.action: Have the Plant Manager or Line 3 supervisor investigate or reward Line 3 for its results.
actions.rationale: They are conflicted, and rewarding the gamed metric reinforces the distortion.

actions.action: Credit and expand the training program as the source of quality gains, or blame the new tubing supplier and revert it.
actions.rationale: The evidence does not support either explanation, so both would misdirect resources.

actions.action: Rebuild a protected reporting channel: anonymous reporting independent of plant management, non-retaliation assurance, and review of the night-shift moves for NCR writers.
actions.rationale: The pulse survey and interviews show a climate of fear that will keep hiding problems.

nextEvidence: Independent audit of Line 3: back-cage inspection, device history records vs component issuance and scrap, and traceability of reworked lots shipped since June
Per-line replacement component and scrap purchasing and issuance data, plus defect and leak rates from the QC lab and complaints by line, shift and operator for Feb-Oct 2026
Who directed the lending of technicians, the reasons for the night-shift moves of former NCR writers, and further anonymous interviews
output.summary: The zero-deviation record is most likely a reporting artifact: the February 2026 bonus rule deducts supervisors' pay per deviation, and reports stopped immediately. Independent measures show quality worsening: complaints rose from 11 to 31 ppm and QC rejections from 0.8% to 1.3%, with luer-bond leaks concentrated on Line 3 lots. Line 3's 118% comes from borrowed technicians; its productivity per technician-hour is flat. The training program and the new tubing do not explain the pattern. Do not replicate Line 3. Suspend the penalty, independently audit Line 3, assess containment and regulatory exposure, and close the open bonding CAPA.
